key_claims: CIA assessed that all credible intelligence linked the Nairobi and Dar es Salaam bombings to Bin Ladin and the Egyptian groups al-Jihad and al-Gama'at al-Islamiyya.
Bin Ladin aimed at a worldwide Islamic government by liberating Saudi Arabia and Palestine and fighting 'dictators'.
Bin Ladin's network was assessed to have ties to extremists across Africa, the Middle East, Southeast Asia, the Balkans, the Caucasus, Central Asia, Kashmir, North America and Europe.
Retaliation for a strike on Bin Ladin at Khowst was judged virtually assured, with anti-US violence in Pakistan likely.
Camps at Khowst train a broad range of nationalities, so a strike could affect Islamic extremists allied with Bin Ladin.
Bin Ladin's death could split his organization into factions, and a lack of central authority could prompt quick retaliation.
